transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um, well, I came in because I just feel wound up almost all the time. It's... it's like my body is constantly bracing for the next bad thing to happen. Even when I'm just sitting at my desk working, or trying to go out and enjoy dance night, I just can't seem to shake it. I'm just tense all the time.
Do you experience sudden, intense surges of fear or discomfort that peak within a few minutes and then subside, or is your feeling of being 'wound up' more of a constant background state?

No, I don't really get sudden, intense surges like that. It's not a panic thing that comes and goes in a few minutes. It's definitely more of a constant background state. Just... always there, humming in the background, keeping me tense.

When you feel this way, do you find that your mind is constantly racing with worries about various different aspects of your life, like work, your health, or your finances, that you find hard to stop?

Yeah, it really does. It's... it's very hard to turn off. My worry doesn't just stay on one thing, like my condo, anymore. It just jumps around. One minute I'm stressing over whether my cousin is upset with me, and then I'm worrying about making a mistake on a support call at work. And then... then it shifts to how I'm ever going to save money or just move forward with my life. It just constantly bounces from one thing to the next.
